name: Knoevenagel condensation with decarboxylation: formaldehyde + malonic acid -> acrylic acid + CO2 + water (dimethylamine catalyst model)

prompt.query: Determine the mechanism of the following reaction: Knoevenagel condensation with decarboxylation: formaldehyde + malonic acid -> acrylic acid + CO2 + water (dimethylamine catalyst model). Reactant SMILES: C=O.O=C(O)CC(=O)O.CNC; product SMILES: C=CC(=O)O.C(=O)=O.O.CNC; total charge 0, multiplicity 1; conditions: piperidine/acetic acid catalysis (modeled here as dimethylamine CNC, written into the SMILES on both sides), reflux. Atom-mapped reactant SMILES: [CH2:1]=[O:2].[CH:3]([H:4])([C:5](=[O:6])[O:7][H:8])[C:9](=[O:10])[OH:11].[CH3:14][N:12]([H:13])[CH3:15]. The 1-based map numbers in it are the indexing convention for `bond_changes` (keep using the plain SMILES above for graph nodes and evidence annotations). The reaction may proceed through a multi-step network: represent each intermediate you identify as a node and each elementary step as an edge; competing pathways you investigate deserve their own edges. You must maintain `mechanism_graph.json` in the sandbox root recording the mechanism graph: nodes (reactant/intermediate/product/transition_state, with SMILES) and elementary-step edges (with `via` pointing to the TS node id). Start the graph at the reactant complex (the pre-reaction complex), not at the separated reactants. The scorer checks that your graph covers the reference mechanism as a subgraph: extra nodes or edges beyond the reference are never penalized, so record every step you actually investigated. Every elementary-step edge must carry `bond_changes`: `break`/`form` lists of [i, j] atom-map index pairs, where [i, j] belongs to `break` if the bond order between atoms i and j decreases over the step (including full cleavage) and to `form` if it increases (including newly formed bonds); a purely conformational or inversion step carries two empty lists. The scorer reads this file forensically; a missing or unparseable file severely impacts the score. Every computational evidence file you produce for a species or step (QM input or log) must carry a `smiles: <SMILES>` comment line identifying the species, so the scorer can bind each graph element to concrete evidence. In your final summary you must report the computed barrier in kcal/mol for the rate-determining step, relative to the reactant complex (the pre-reaction complex, e.g. the ion-dipole complex of a bimolecular reaction; for a unimolecular process this is simply the reactant minimum). Run the computations with ORCA or Gaussian: the scorer parses only these two programs' log formats, so output from any other program cannot count as evidence. Allowed computational methods are limited to MACE-OMol25 and xTB; calls beyond the whitelist are intercepted.

system.conditions: piperidine/acetic acid catalysis (modeled here as dimethylamine CNC, written into the SMILES on both sides), reflux

edges.step_type: direct condensation of formaldehyde with dimethylamine -> iminium [CH2=NMe2]+ + OH- (C=N forms, C=O and N-H break, carbinolamine not a separate node)
OH- deprotonates the central C-H of malonic acid -> water + malonic alpha-carbanion (-1)
carbanion attacks the iminium carbon (C-C bond formation, C=N pi breaks) -> 3-(dimethylamino)malonic acid adduct
decarboxylation via a six-membered cyclic TS: C-C(OOH) cleavage with concerted proton transfer from the carboxyl O-H to the central carbon -> 3-(dimethylamino)propanoic acid + CO2
elimination of dimethylamine: C-N cleavage with alpha-C-H transfer onto nitrogen and C=C pi formation -> acrylic acid
